=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md: Step 1 "Cleanup calls" paragraph (lines 41-42) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: In `start — restart` mode, a denied deletion of the previous pickup's hourly trigger is skipped, but the current pickup still creates its own trigger and processes the queue, allowing concurrent pickups to start duplicate sessions for the same item.
  WHY: Both pickups can read the same still-open queue item before either closes it; the queue item is closed only after session creation succeeds.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: Hand-back step 1 (around line 249) | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: The safety-net trigger deletion lacks the required `get_trigger` ownership verification before `delete_trigger`.
  WHY: Without verifying the trigger name and `persistent_session_id`, a stale or repurposed ID could cause deletion of a trigger owned by another session.
- CLAUDE.md: §26.D terminal path (lines 1984-1985) | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: The terminal-path fixer instruction deletes the fired hand-back Routine by ID without instructing the fixer to call `get_trigger` to verify ownership first.
  WHY: §26.I requires ownership verification for triggers identified by ID, including a checker's own hand-back trigger.
- CLAUDE.md: §26.C step 5 "Terminal, fixer gone" fallback (line 1953) | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: The fallback deletes the fixer's hand-back Routine by ID without the `get_trigger` ownership verification required by §26.I.
  WHY: The fallback delete lacks the required check, leaving the procedure inconsistent with the cleanup-call safety contract.
- .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md, .claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md, .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: Entire files; PR diff hunks in all three root files; All hunks editing root `.claude/commands/*.md` files (pickup: lines 38-89, fix-claude-pr: lines 60-75, implement-plan-claude: lines 8-425) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The PR edits active root `.claude/commands/*` files despite the PR description's twin-first requirement that these root copies are not changed by the PR.
  WHY: The root command files are executable instructions, and direct edits bypass the declared twin-sync or sync-blocker delivery process; the reviewers differ on the operational risk of this discrepancy.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: Hand-back step 1 (around line 249) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The implementation of §26.I cleanup-call skipping for the safety-net trigger deletion does not include the required get_trigger ownership verification before delete_trigger.
  WHY: The safety-net ID comes from the arming report. Without ownership verification (checking name and persistent_session_id), a stale or repurposed ID could lead to deleting a trigger owned by another session, which §26.I is specifically designed to prevent. The prose ownership claim in the file is insufficient; the mandatory get_trigger check is missing.
- CLAUDE.md: §26.D terminal path (lines 1984-1985) | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The terminal-path fixer instruction deletes the fired hand-back Routine by ID without instructing the fixer to call get_trigger to verify ownership first.
  WHY: §26.I requires ownership verification for triggers identified by ID, including a checker's own hand-back trigger. Although the trigger was recently fired in this session, the rule makes no exception for "just fired" triggers, and the omission is inconsistent with the safety invariant defined in the new §26.I section.
- CLAUDE.md: §26.C step 5 "Terminal, fixer gone" fallback (line 1953) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The fallback deletes the fixer's hand-back Routine by ID without the get_trigger ownership verification required by §26.I.
  WHY: The §26.I rule mandates get_trigger verification for a checker's own hand-back trigger. The fallback delete lacks this check, leaving the procedure inconsistent with the required cleanup-call safety contract.
- .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md: lines 41, 69, 78, 86 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: In `start — restart` mode, if deleting the previous pickup’s trigger is denied, the instructions skip the remaining cleanup but still create this session’s hourly trigger.
  WHY: Both pickup sessions can process the same open queue item before either closes it, starting duplicate sessions for the same issue or PR.
- .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md, .claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md, .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: Entire files | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The PR edits active root command files directly, violating the documented "twin-first" requirement and the PR's own description.
  WHY: These root files are executable instructions for the sessions that use them. Changes made directly to these files bypass the documented twin-sync process, leaving the twin files (if any) and the root files out of sync. This makes the intended "twin-first" process unfalsifiable, and a future revert or change to the twins would not correctly propagate to the active root files.
